headings: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
Whether it be stolen or no.
It will be (or is intended to be stolen.)

units.short_original_anchor: Of a Thief and Theft.
units.normalized_historical_statement: This heading begins the requested theft material on printed page 330.

units.short_original_anchor: Haly saith, you must know that the ascendant is the Signifi-
units.normalized_historical_statement: The passage attributes to Haly the assignment of the ascendant as significator of the querent.
preconditions: A question concerning theft or something taken away.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The anchor retains the printed line-ending division of Significator.

units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the second is Significator of the
units.normalized_historical_statement: In the method attributed to Haly, the lord of the second signifies the thing stolen or taken away.
preconditions: A question concerning theft or something taken away.

units.short_original_anchor: and the seventh house is the Significator of the Thiefe
units.normalized_historical_statement: In the method attributed to Haly, the seventh house signifies the thief if there is no peregrine planet in an angle or second house.
preconditions: No peregrine planet is in an angle or second house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The following paragraph supplies an alternative priority for a peregrine planet.

units.short_original_anchor: the tenth house is the Signifier of the
units.normalized_historical_statement: The tenth house signifies the king. The sentence continues across the page boundary: the sign of the fourth signifies the place where the thing is, or from which it was taken away.
preconditions: The theft method attributed to Haly.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The original errata leaf has an entry for printed page 330, line 6, directing the reading 'of'; the visible body text already reads 'of the' here.
The bottom catchword 'King,' repeats the opening word on printed page 331.

units.short_original_anchor: you must know from the Lords of those houses
units.normalized_historical_statement: The reader is directed to learn the proper significations from the lords of the assigned houses, thereby judging the condition and state of what is missing.
preconditions: The preceding assignments of houses and significators.

units.short_original_anchor: if you find in the ascendant a Planet peregrine
units.normalized_historical_statement: A peregrine planet in the ascendant is to be taken as significator of the thief, especially if it is lord of the seventh house.
preconditions: A peregrine planet is in the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Being lord of the seventh strengthens this assignment; it is not stated as necessary.

units.short_original_anchor: but if no Planet be in the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: If there is no planet in the ascendant, inspect the other angles and assign a planet found there as significator of the thief.
preconditions: No planet is in the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This clause does not explicitly repeat the peregrine qualification.

units.short_original_anchor: This shall be more copiously handled in some Chapters following.
units.normalized_historical_statement: A marginal note promises fuller treatment in following chapters and calls the present method 'A most certain rule.'
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is the historical author's assessment of the rule.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.normalized_historical_statement: A separate subsection addresses selection of the thief's significator.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh commonly signifies the Thief
units.normalized_historical_statement: The lord of the seventh commonly signifies the thief, especially when peregrine in the ascendant or another angle.
preconditions: A theft question.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Peregrinity and angular placement strengthen the common assignment.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: then behold if any other Planet be pe-
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the seventh does not meet the preceding description, take another peregrine planet in an angle as the thief.
preconditions: The lord of the seventh is not as described in the preceding rule.
Another planet is peregrine in an angle.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed 'if he be not so' refers back to the preceding combined description.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: take the Lord of the hour, and call
units.normalized_historical_statement: If no planet is peregrine in any angle, take the lord of the hour as the thief.
preconditions: No planet is peregrine in any angle.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the fourth be Lord of the seventh
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the fourth is also lord of the seventh and is in the ascendant, the author calls the indication more radical and identifies the querent as the thief. He restricts this rule to cases in which suspicion concerns the querent's fidelity or the querent is most suspected.
preconditions: The lord of the fourth is also lord of the seventh.
That lord is in the ascendant.
Suspicion concerns the querent's fidelity, or the querent is the most suspected person.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This records a historical astrological accusation rule, not evidence of an actual theft.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: whose complexion and condition is ac-
units.normalized_historical_statement: The complexion and condition of the person described in the preceding rule are assigned according to the planet ruling the seventh and its sign.
preconditions: The preceding restricted identification of the querent as thief.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No specific complexion or condition is supplied on these pages.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: A Planet is then peregrin when he is
units.normalized_historical_statement: The marginal definition calls a planet peregrine when it is in none of its own house, triplicity, term, exaltation or face.
preconditions: Determining whether a candidate planet is peregrine.

units.section_heading: Of the SIGNIFICATOR of the Thiefe.
units.short_original_anchor: I rather and more assured- ly prefer the
units.normalized_historical_statement: A marginal authorial preference favors the lord of the seventh as a more rational and conscientious significator, qualifying the alternative selection methods in the body text.
preconditions: Choosing the thief's significator.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The anchor preserves the visible division of 'assuredly'.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.normalized_historical_statement: A separate subsection addresses the stolen object's significator.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: The Significator of the thing stolen is the Lord of the Term
units.normalized_historical_statement: The starred rule assigns the stolen object's significator to the lord of the term occupied by the Moon.
preconditions: Determining the significator of the stolen thing.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This differs from the second-house-lord assignment elsewhere in the window.
The adjoining starred marginal note explicitly discounts this rule.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: This rule is vulgar, and not of any cre-
units.normalized_historical_statement: The starred marginal note calls the Moon's term-lord rule vulgar and of no credit.
preconditions: The starred rule assigning the stolen object to the Moon's term lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The criticism belongs specifically to the starred rule.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: the ascendant is Signifier of the question, or Demandant
units.normalized_historical_statement: After finding the thief's significator and understanding its disposition from the significant planet and its aspects, treat the ascendant as significator of the question or demandant.
preconditions: The thief's significator has been found.
Its disposition has been considered through the planet and its aspects.

units.section_heading: The SIGNIFICATOR of the thing stolen.
units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the ascendant draw towards the Lord
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the ascendant draws toward the lord of the seventh or lord of the hour, or is in the seventh, the author judges that the thief will be taken soon afterward or that recovery of the lost thing is hoped for.
preconditions: The lord of the ascendant draws toward the lord of the seventh, draws toward the lord of the hour, or occupies the seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source offers capture or hope of recovery as alternatives, not guaranteed recovery.

units.short_original_anchor: Of THEFTS.
units.normalized_historical_statement: This heading begins another set of theft rules.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The heading contains fewer than five words.

units.short_original_anchor: The first house, which is the ascendant, is for the querent
units.normalized_historical_statement: The first house, or ascendant, represents the querent, and its lord represents the person who has lost the goods. The sentence continues onto printed page 332.
preconditions: A theft or lost-goods question.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The bottom catchword 'his' repeats the first word on the next page.

units.short_original_anchor: his Lord for him that hath lost the Goods
units.normalized_historical_statement: The opening continuation assigns 'his Lord' to the person who has lost the goods and to the place from which the goods were taken. The antecedent of 'his' lies before this window.
preconditions: Continuation of a significator assignment begun on the preceding page.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The preceding words are unavailable in this window; the antecedent must not be supplied from memory.

units.short_original_anchor: the seventh house and his Lord, and the peregrine Planet
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh house and its lord, a peregrine planet in an angle, and the lord of the hour signify the thief or party who took away the goods.
preconditions: The peregrine planet specified here is in an angle.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No priority among these thief significators is stated in the visible continuation.

units.short_original_anchor: This is a very good judgment, and may well be trusted
units.normalized_historical_statement: A printed marginal note endorses the adjacent judgment as very good and trustworthy.
preconditions: The note accompanies the opening passage on printed page 332.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Its precise scope within the surrounding rules is not expressly delimited.

units.short_original_anchor: shall signifie the Goods or thing that is lost
units.normalized_historical_statement: The second house, its lord, and the Moon signify the goods or thing that is lost, stolen, or missing.
preconditions: A question concerns lost, stolen, or missing goods.

units.short_original_anchor: the fourth house and his Lord shall signifie the place
units.normalized_historical_statement: The fourth house and its lord signify the place where the goods were laid, put, done, or conveyed, and where they are at that instant.
preconditions: A question concerns the location of the goods.

units.short_original_anchor: shall tell and shew whether the Goods shall be found
units.normalized_historical_statement: The aspects of the Sun and Moon, the lord of the ascendant, the lord of the second, and the lord of the Moon's house to the lord of the ascendant, together with their applications and aspects to one another, indicate whether the goods will be found or recovered.
preconditions: Examine the named significators' aspects and applications.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The sentence's punctuation does not clearly delimit every member of the aspect list.

units.short_original_anchor: then is the Goods taken away by somebody
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the second and the Moon are in the seventh, in the sign of the seventh, and the lord of the seventh beholds them by trine or sextile, the goods have been taken away by somebody rather than simply lost.
preconditions: Lord of the second and Moon in the seventh, in the sign of the seventh.
Lord of the seventh beholds them by trine or sextile.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source permits the aspect to be 'long out', explaining this as many degrees distant.

units.short_original_anchor: it is neither lost nor stolen, but carelesly mislaid
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the second, occupies the house of the lord of the hour, and goes to conjunction with the lord of the seventh, the party left the goods somewhere they had been and forgot them; the goods are carelessly mislaid.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the second.
Moon is in the house of the lord of the hour.
Moon is going to conjunction with the lord of the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: the thing is not stolen, but taken away in jest
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the ascendant and is in the fourth, while the lord of the second is in the seventh or in the sign of the eighth house, in conjunction to the second house and sextile or trine to the Moon, the thing was taken away in jest.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the ascendant and in the fourth.
Lord of the second is in the seventh or in the sign of the eighth house.
The printed text also requires conjunction 'to the second house'.
Sextile or trine to the Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The unusual expression 'in conjunction to the second house' is retained without silently substituting another target.

units.short_original_anchor: then is the Goods stolen and taken away
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the ascendant and is in the ascendant, not far remote, and the Sun rules the second and is in the third with the lord of the seventh, while the lord of the seventh oppresses the Moon by square, the goods are stolen and taken away.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the ascendant and in the ascendant, 'not farre remote'.
Sun is lord of the second and in the third with the lord of the seventh.
Lord of the seventh oppresses the Moon with a square.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The reference point of 'not farre remote' is not further explained.

units.short_original_anchor: Lord of the second also being Lord of the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon is in the third and oppressed by the lord of the seventh through his square aspect, and the lord of the second also rules the ascendant and is in the seventh, in the sign of the seventh, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: Moon in the third.
Lord of the seventh oppresses the Moon by square.
Lord of the second also rules the ascendant.
That lord is in the seventh, in the sign of the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: except the Sun and Moon behold the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: Within the preceding configuration, if the thing was taken in jest, recovery will be difficult unless the Sun and Moon behold the ascendant.
preconditions: The configuration of A2011.
The thing was taken in jest.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The Sun and Moon beholding the ascendant provide the stated exception to difficult recovery.
The anchor renders the printed solar and lunar glyphs as their names; the literal image has glyphs.

units.short_original_anchor: but overlooked and mistaken
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon is 'the seventh' in the sign of the lord of the hour, and the lord of the hour rules the seventh, the goods are overlooked and mistaken rather than stolen or taken away.
preconditions: The Moon is described as 'the seventh' in the sign of the lord of the hour.
Lord of the hour is lord of the seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed opening appears to omit 'in' before 'the seventh'.
The short anchor is only four words because this diagnostic phrase is especially clear.

units.short_original_anchor: then hath the party lost the Goods as he went
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon is in the fifth in Capricorn and rules the hour, Venus rules the second and is in the tenth in the sign of the seventh, and the Moon is in conjunction with the lord of the seventh, the party lost the goods while travelling or left them in a place they visited.
preconditions: Moon in the fifth and in Capricorn.
Moon is Lady of the hour.
Venus is Lady of the second, in the tenth, in the sign of the seventh.
Moon in conjunction with the lord of the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: taken away in jest by the Master of the house
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the hour and is in Cancer in the eighth, the lord of the second is in the fifth, neither beholds the lord of the seventh, and the lord of the seventh is in the seventh, the master of the house took the goods in jest and will deny doing so.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the hour, in Cancer, in the eighth.
Lord of the second in the fifth.
Neither Moon nor lord of the second beholds the lord of the seventh.
Lord of the seventh in the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: then hath somebody taken the things away in jest
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the hour, is in the fourth, and is conjunct the lord of the seventh, while the lord of the second is in the twelfth and sextile the lord of the seventh, somebody took the things in jest.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the hour and in the fourth.
Moon conjunct the lord of the seventh.
Lord of the second in the twelfth.
Lord of the second sextile the lord of the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: then is the Goods taken away in jest
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon is in the sign of the lord of the seventh without beholding that lord, the Moon is in the twelfth, and the lord of the second is in the sixth, the goods were taken away in jest.
preconditions: Moon in the sign of the lord of the seventh.
Moon does not behold the lord of the seventh.
Moon in the twelfth.
Lord of the second in the sixth.

units.short_original_anchor: but will soone be had again
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the second last separated from the lord of the Moon's house, the goods were stolen in jest and will soon be recovered.
preconditions: Lord of the second last separated from the lord of the house occupied by the Moon.

units.short_original_anchor: the Goods is taken away and stolen by somebody
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon separates from the lord of the second by square, somebody has taken away and stolen the goods.
preconditions: Moon separates from the lord of the second by square.

units.short_original_anchor: separate from the lord of the house where in she is
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the second and separates from the lord of the house she occupies, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the second.
Moon separates from the lord of her occupied house.

units.short_original_anchor: then did the Querent lay it downe and forget it
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the ascendant separates from Jupiter or from the lord of the second house, the querent laid the thing down and forgot it, thereby losing it.
preconditions: Lord of the ascendant separates from Jupiter or from the lord of the second.

units.short_original_anchor: it is the surer
units.normalized_historical_statement: The foregoing judgment that the querent laid the thing down and forgot it is more certain when both the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the second separate from Jupiter.
preconditions: Both the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the second separate from Jupiter.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The diagnostic phrase contains only four words; its antecedent is A2021.

units.short_original_anchor: doth apply unto the lord of the second house
units.normalized_historical_statement: Another configuration supporting the foregoing judgment has the Moon ruling the ascendant, separating from Jupiter, and applying to the lord of the second, which also last separated from Jupiter.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the ascendant.
Moon separates from Jupiter.
Moon applies to the lord of the second.
Lord of the second also last separated from Jupiter.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source says these configurations give one judgment, referring back to laying down and forgetting the goods.

units.short_original_anchor: yet if it be so, it giveth all one judgment
units.normalized_historical_statement: The same judgment applies when the lord of the ascendant, exemplified by the Sun, also rules the second and separates from Jupiter.
preconditions: One planet rules both ascendant and second.
That planet separates from Jupiter.
The source names the Sun in its parenthetical example.

units.short_original_anchor: then did the party lose the Goods by the way
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the second or Jupiter separates from the lord of the ascendant, the party lost the goods along their route, in a place they visited, or through their slipping privately from a pocket into a secret place; they are neither stolen nor found.
preconditions: Lord of the second or Jupiter separates from the lord of the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source lists alternative circumstances without selecting one.

units.short_original_anchor: then is the Goods absolutely stolen
units.normalized_historical_statement: If none of the foregoing separations exists, examine whether the peregrine planet, lord of the seventh, or Mercury acting for the thief applies to Jupiter or the lord of the second. If so, the goods are absolutely stolen and the thief came intending to steal.
preconditions: None of the separations previously described.
Peregrine planet, lord of the seventh, or Mercury as thief applies to Jupiter or the lord of the second.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The sentence begins on PDF367 and continues on PDF368.
Mercury is expressly qualified here as a thief significator.

units.short_original_anchor: did offer it selfe to the Thiefe
units.normalized_historical_statement: Under the preceding absence of separations, if the lord of the second or Jupiter applies to the peregrine planet, lord of the seventh, or Mercury as thief, the goods offered themselves to the thief or were easily obtained. The taker came without an intention to steal, but saw the thing lying openly and carelessly, then took it away.
preconditions: Continuation of the examination introduced when the foregoing separations are absent.
Lord of the second or Jupiter applies to a named thief significator.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Application direction reverses A2026 and changes the attributed intention.

units.short_original_anchor: then the Querent did lose the thing by the way
units.normalized_historical_statement: The querent lost the thing while travelling, and it was not stolen, under the printed compound configuration: the Moon rules both ascendant and second, is in Taurus, and applies by conjunction to the Sun within one degree; the Sun rules the third; Mars is the peregrine planet and is in the tenth; Mercury applies to Mars; and none of the aforesaid separations or applications impedes. The passage additionally says 'or the lord of the seventh in the third' before its conclusion.
preconditions: Moon rules ascendant and second.
Moon in Taurus, applying by conjunction to the Sun within one degree.
Sun is lord of the third.
Mars is the peregrine planet and in the tenth.
Mercury applies to Mars.
No aforesaid separation or application impedes.
Printed additional alternative: lord of the seventh in the third.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The scope of the final 'or' is ambiguous; the source does not clearly establish whether it replaces the whole preceding configuration or only its immediately preceding clause.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.normalized_historical_statement: A new named section considers whether the thing is stolen.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: Signifier of the Thiefe be in the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the thief's significator is in the ascendant, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: Thief's significator in the ascendant.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: or give his vertue to the
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the thief's significator gives his virtue to the Moon, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: Thief's significator gives virtue to the Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The exact short anchor ends before the printed lunar glyph.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: to him, it is stolen
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon gives her virtue to the thief's significator, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: Moon gives virtue to the thief's significator.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: give his vertue to the Signifier of the Thiefe
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the ascendant gives his virtue to the thief's significator, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: Lord of the ascendant gives virtue to the thief's significator.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: if the Signifier behold the lord of the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the thief's significator beholds the lord of the ascendant by square or opposition, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: Thief's significator square or opposite the lord of the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: 'Signifier' refers back to the thief's significator.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: if the Signifier behold the lord
units.normalized_historical_statement: The same theft judgment is given if the thief's significator beholds the Moon by conjunction, square, or opposition.
preconditions: Thief's significator conjunct, square, or opposite the Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This target and its three aspect glyphs follow the quoted anchor in the same sentence.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: or the lord of the house of the Moon
units.normalized_historical_statement: The sentence also lists the lord of the Moon's house as a target whose being beheld by the thief's significator indicates theft.
preconditions: Thief's significator beholds the lord of the Moon's house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No fresh aspect glyphs accompany this target; whether the preceding conjunction, square, and opposition list carries over is not explicit.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: or the lord of the Terme of the Moon
units.normalized_historical_statement: The lord of the Moon's term is another listed target in the same theft-indicating aspect sentence.
preconditions: Thief's significator beholds the lord of the Moon's term.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No fresh aspect glyphs accompany this target; carry-over of the preceding aspect list is not explicit.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: or the lord of the second house
units.normalized_historical_statement: The lord of the second house is another listed target in the same theft-indicating aspect sentence.
preconditions: Thief's significator beholds the lord of the second house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No fresh aspect glyphs accompany this target; carry-over of the preceding aspect list is not explicit.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: or his lord, the thing is stolen
units.normalized_historical_statement: The Part of Fortune or its lord is also a listed target in the same theft-indicating aspect sentence.
preconditions: Thief's significator beholds the Part of Fortune or its lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed circled-cross glyph is read as the Part of Fortune.
No fresh aspect glyphs accompany this target; carry-over of the preceding aspect list is not explicit.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: And if any Planet be in the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: If any planet in the ascendant gives its power to the thief's significator, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: A planet is in the ascendant.
That planet gives power to the thief's significator.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: or the Significator to him by
units.normalized_historical_statement: The converse relation also indicates theft: the thief's significator gives power to the planet in the ascendant by square or opposition.
preconditions: A planet is in the ascendant.
Thief's significator gives power to that planet by square or opposition.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The placement of the square and opposition glyphs explicitly follows the converse clause; their application to the preceding direction is not separately stated.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: if some of these constellations be not
units.normalized_historical_statement: If some of the foregoing constellations are absent, the thing is not stolen, subject to the ensuing list of infortunes and unfortunate significators.
preconditions: Some of the foregoing constellations are absent.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source says 'some', without defining how many absences suffice.
The exceptions are finally described as signifying loss or losing, without an explicit renewed declaration of theft.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: except there be an Infortune in the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: An Infortune in the ascendant or second house is an exception to the preceding not-stolen judgment; the source includes it among configurations signifying loss or losing.
preconditions: An Infortune occupies the ascendant or second house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The conclusion expressly says loss or losing, rather than expressly identifying a theft.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the house of the Moon
units.normalized_historical_statement: An unfortunate lord of the Moon's house is another exception in the list signifying loss or losing.
preconditions: Lord of the Moon's house is unfortunate.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not specify an aspect or particular mode of being unfortunate.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: or of the Terme of the Moon is unfortunate
units.normalized_historical_statement: An unfortunate lord of the Moon's term is another exception signifying loss or losing.
preconditions: Lord of the Moon's term is unfortunate.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not specify an aspect or particular mode of being unfortunate.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: or his lord be unfortunate
units.normalized_historical_statement: An unfortunate Part of Fortune or its lord is another exception signifying loss or losing.
preconditions: Part of Fortune or its lord is unfortunate.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The circled-cross glyph precedes the anchor.
The source does not specify an aspect or particular mode of being unfortunate.

units.section_heading: Whether it be stolen or no.
units.short_original_anchor: or the lord of the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: An infortunate lord of the ascendant is another exception signifying loss or losing.
preconditions: Lord of the ascendant is infortunate.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The predicate 'be infortunate' follows the next coordinated target in the source.
